function: Joint CSI acquisition and RIS phase-shift design: diffusion model imputes the full cascaded channel from partial CSI, decision transformer outputs RIS phase shifts maximizing cumulative rate (p. 6-8).
system: Downlink: BS with M=4 antennas, passive reflecting RIS with N=64, 256 or 512 elements, single-antenna user, direct link blocked, flat fading; no carrier frequency stated (p. 4, 12).
method: Conditional diffusion model with spatial feature Transformer for channel imputation; decision Transformer supervised-pre-trained on DDPG/PPO trajectories, then few-shot fine-tuned (last layer) (p. 6-11).
data_channel: Synthetic spatially correlated complex Gaussian channels with sinc correlation under isotropic scattering; 5000 CSI samples per environment for N=64, 256, 512; default settings of [22] (p. 5, 12).
test_conditions: Offline pre-training on varied BS-RIS distances, scattering intensity and SNR; new environments with changed channel parameters and distances; few-shot fine-tuning of the last DT layer (p. 11-12, 14).
baselines: Random channel fill-in (RC) for the diffusion model; RCDT, PCDT upper bound, DM-PPO, DM-DDPG and RC-PPO; no SDR or AO comparison (p. 12-13).
metrics: NMSE of generated CSI versus SNR and mask ratio (p. 12); effective data rate versus mask ratio, SNR and training epochs (p. 12-14).
complexity: Big-O orders for diffusion model O(K(NpN+N^2)dD) and decision transformer O(L(T^2 l+T l^2)); convergence epochs (300 versus 900); no runtime or FLOPs (p. 11, 13).
q2_support: p. 14: "can quickly generalize and converge and achieve near-optimal performance in new environments under diverse conditions"
q3_support: p. 12: "we use the random channel (RC) approach"; p. 13: "the performance of DEDT surpasses RL methods by approximately 7.5%"
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall complexity is O(K(Np N + N 2 )dD)"
notes: Included. The work solves two functions jointly: CSI acquisition by a conditional diffusion model (area 2, NMSE only in Fig. 5, p. 12) and RIS phase-shift design by a decision transformer (area 3). Area 3 chosen because the objective (Eq. 3, p. 5) and the main comparisons (Figs. 6-10, p. 12-14) use the effective data rate; the paper also calls channel estimation its core contribution (p. 2), so the reviewer may prefer area 2. ris=1: passive reflecting RIS with unit amplitude (p. 1, 4). q1=0: custom spatially correlated model derived under isotropic scattering (p. 5), with no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data. q2=1: the pre-trained decision transformer is fine-tuned with few-shot samples in new environments (p. 11, 14; p. 12: 'we change the channel parameters and BS-RIS distances to simulate different wireless environments'); the paper does not say which environments were held out of pre-training. q3=1, to confirm: the only non-learned baseline is the random channel fill-in (RC, p. 12, described as 'the baseline method'), while SDR and AO are explicitly not compared (p. 13); learned baselines are DM-PPO, DM-DDPG and RC-PPO, compared on effective data rate and convergence (p. 13). q4: big-O orders only (p. 11). q5: synthetic data, no link, DOI or code statement.
